items.name: theme-180connect
items.title: The Meridian (180Connect)
items.description: A contemporary take on professional services, retaining clarity and credibility while making room for character, expression, and a little more ambition.
items.docs: Load the fonts with next/font: Lato({ weight: ["300", "400", "700"], variable: "--font-lato" }); Geist({ variable: "--font-geist-sans" }); Geist_Mono({ variable: "--font-geist-mono" }). Rules: https://bash-ui-registry.vercel.app/systems/180connect

rules.title: The card is a border, not a shadow
rules.body: border border-rule bg-card rounded-panel. Shadows are only for things that float: popovers, dialogs, menus.

rules.title: 10px reads as a document
rules.body: rounded-panel (10px) for cards, rounded-inset (6px) for controls and chips inside them. Never rounded-2xl.

rules.title: Insets are paper, not another white card
rules.body: Recessed content sits on bg-paper with rounded-inset. A border inside a border is noise.

rules.title: Three inks, by meaning
rules.body: ink is content, dim is context about content, faint is furniture. Never set text with opacity.

rules.title: The accent says where you are; states say what is true
rules.body: lead appears in four places only: active tab, links, focus ring, register keys. Buttons are ink. go / hold / stop each carry a dot as well as a colour.

rules.title: Uppercase is for codes only
rules.body: Mono, 10.5px, tracked, faint — for things that really are codes (UK CHARITY, PRIORITY). Never a heading style.

rules.title: Content arrives in reading order
rules.body: Blur-up entrances, staggered by section, never all at once. Reduced motion is honoured everywhere.

items.name: theme-ledge
items.title: Frontier (Ledge)
items.description: An overdue departure from the expected, where expressive design and thoughtful restraint come together to make innovation feel natural, credible, and assured.

light.code-font: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, monospace

items.docs: Load the fonts with next/font: Lora({ variable: "--font-lora", subsets: ["latin"] }); Instrument_Serif({ weight: "400", variable: "--font-instrument-serif", subsets: ["latin"] }). Rules: https://bash-ui-registry.vercel.app/systems/ledge

rules.title: Two serifs, two jobs
rules.body: Instrument Serif (400) gives headings and key financial figures their editorial character. Lora carries body text, labels and controls. Use tabular numerals for aligned amounts; monospace is a registry fallback for code, not the app's financial typeface.

rules.title: Use the current cool app surface
rules.body: Near-white ground, white cards, cool blue-grey insets and slate ink. The landlord, tenant and admin apps all use ledge-cool. Its 16px panels and 10px inputs supersede the older 4px base styles.

rules.title: Hairlines first, shadows lightly
rules.body: Cards use border-rule with rounded-panel and generous padding. A very faint shadow can lift an interactive card; stronger shadows belong to floating dialogs and menus. Use paper for recessed content.

rules.title: Green actions are pills
rules.body: Primary actions use bg-primary text-primary-foreground and rounded-full; hover deepens the green. Secondary actions are outlined pills. Reserve rounded-inset for inputs and inner surfaces. Links, selected dates and the brand's terminal dot use lead.

rules.title: Labels whisper; headings read naturally
rules.body: Small section eyebrows and field labels may be uppercase with 0.08–0.25em tracking. Headings stay in sentence case with tight leading. Use dim for explanatory copy and faint for quiet labels and furniture.

rules.title: Financial colour has a meaning
rules.body: Green marks collected or paid, gold marks pending or outstanding, and red marks overdue or failed. Pair each colour with a label. Charts distinguish landlord funds in emerald, Ledge revenue in gold and processing fees in clay; avoid decorative rainbow series.

rules.title: Leave room to read
rules.body: Use a centred reading column (48rem tenant, 56rem landlord, 64rem admin), roughly 24px side gutters and 48px main vertical padding. Separate sections generously; group related ledger rows with fine dividers. Subtle ruled lines and dotted leaders are optional ledger details.

rules.title: Motion follows the ledger
rules.body: Sections rise and fade in reading order; chart bars grow from their baseline and arcs draw on. Keep hover changes near 200ms and entrances around 700–900ms. Honour reduced motion with useReducedMotionConfig() when implementing registry components.

rules.title: Dark mode is a bash-ui adaptation
rules.body: Ledge's app supplies the light palette only. This entry derives dark slate surfaces, pale ink, lifted green actions and brighter state colours for the gallery's dark mode. Additional contract colours and ranked chart ramps are palette extensions rather than original Ledge tokens.

items.name: theme-portfolio
items.title: Understated (Portfolio)
items.description: Minimal by intention, expressive by nature. Considered typography, generous white space, and subtle artistic details create a distinctive visual identity that lets the work speak for itself.

light.code-font: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, monospace

rules.title: Expressive headings, rounded copy
rules.body: Use Viaoda Libre for the introductory statement and section headings, and Open Runde for paragraphs, metadata, project captions and controls. The original Viaoda font ships at 400; keep its distinctive silhouette rather than substituting a generic serif. Geist is the source's default UI fallback; monospace is a registry fallback for technical content.

rules.title: Let the work carry the colour
rules.body: Keep the page white, main copy black and supporting information zinc grey. Primary actions and navigation are monochrome. Project imagery, technology marks and the GitHub activity chart supply colour; do not invent a saturated structural accent.

rules.title: Space is the main separator
rules.body: Use broad gutters (8% on small screens, 18% on desktop), generous section gaps and alternating image-and-text rows. Centre the introduction on mobile and align it to the left on desktop. Most text sections sit directly on the page rather than inside cards.

rules.title: Rounded frames, circular actions
rules.body: The source's base radius is 10px. Project media uses rounded-2xl, which resolves to 18px through its radius scale; use rounded-panel for those frames and rounded-inset (10px) for controls. Navigation, collaboration buttons and arrow badges use fully rounded pills or circles.

rules.title: A warm wash is an occasional material
rules.body: Certification panels use a pale warm wash with irregular, layered watercolour edges. Use paper for this warmth and keep the main page neutral. Hand-drawn marks, small image rotations and tiny raised icon tiles are accents, not a treatment for every surface.

rules.title: Hierarchy comes from type and tone
rules.body: Keep headings in sentence case. Use black for names and emphasis, dim for supporting descriptions and faint for incidental furniture. Introductory text grows from roughly 14px to 20px; major headings reach roughly 48px. Use italics sparingly for roles and qualifications.

rules.title: Motion lives in the controls
rules.body: Calls to action slide their circular arrow across the pill over about 500ms. Navigation expands with damped springs; small tooltips fade around 200ms. When extracting components later, use motion/react and honour useReducedMotionConfig(); the source's motion does not consistently provide reduced-motion handling.

rules.title: Distinguish source tokens from extensions
rules.body: The source defines neutral light and dark UI tokens, but its portfolio sections keep fixed white backgrounds and black text. This entry applies those dark tokens consistently for the gallery and derives a dark warm inset. Positive, waiting, financial and frosted-menu slots extend the contract; they are not evidence of additional Portfolio components or an original financial palette.

items.name: theme-steeze
items.title: Curated (Steeze)
items.description: A refined visual identity that feels elevated without feeling exclusive. Thoughtful design gives it a distinctive presence while keeping it welcoming and approachable.
items.docs: Load the fonts with next/font: DM_Sans({ variable: "--font-dm-sans", subsets: ["latin"] }); Playfair_Display({ variable: "--font-playfair-display", subsets: ["latin"], style: ["normal", "italic"] }); Orbitron({ variable: "--font-orbitron", subsets: ["latin"] }); Outfit({ variable: "--font-outfit", subsets: ["latin"] }). Rules: https://bash-ui-registry.vercel.app/systems/steeze

rules.title: Playfair speaks, DM Sans explains
rules.body: Playfair Display is the page's root face: wordmark, headings, navigation and button labels. DM Sans carries paragraphs, answers, form copy and the footer. Section headings request weight 300, which renders as Playfair's lightest available weight (400); the hero uses 500 and small card titles 600 in uppercase. Body copy often sits at DM Sans 300 with 1.5–1.6 line height.

rules.title: Charcoal and cream, nothing else neutral
rules.body: The ground is #222222 and the ink is #f1efe0; light mode swaps them, as the landing's cream sections do. Derive every other neutral from those two at reduced strength: borders at 10–15%, quiet fills at 2–5%, supporting text at 60–70%. Never use pure white text or a grey from another scale.

rules.title: Tight serifs, spaced labels
rules.body: Large headings pull in tracking (about −1 to −2px at 32–64px) with 1.1–1.2 leading and stay in sentence case. Italicise one phrase for emphasis, as in "Join the culture". Small eyebrows, numbering (01, 02…) and footer captions go uppercase with +0.05em to 1px tracking.

rules.title: Actions are pills
rules.body: Primary calls to action are rounded-full pills in Playfair: cream fill with charcoal label, or a cream outline in the navigation. On hover, a small dot expands to fill the pill and the label gives way to an up-right arrow over about 300ms. Inputs and inner controls use rounded-inset (8px), cards rounded-panel (12px) and full-screen dialogs about 16px.

rules.title: Hairlines, not boxes
rules.body: Cards barely lift from the ground: a near-invisible fill with a border-rule hairline. Lists and accordions separate items with bottom borders only. Reserve deep, soft black shadows for floating media such as phone mock-ups; do not add decorative shadows to cards.

rules.title: Lilac is a glow, used sparingly
rules.body: Lead is the lilac from the page glow and the app's on-switches, spinners and default-address badges. Use it for links, focus, selection and small marks, never for large fills or body text. Primary buttons stay cream on charcoal (or charcoal on cream). In light mode, lead deepens so it reads as text on cream.

rules.title: Status in soft pastels
rules.body: Steeze's internal dashboards mark good in mint, warning in gold and bad in rose, and rank in gold, silver and bronze. Pair each with a label. On charcoal the pastels are used as-is; on cream this entry deepens them so they pass as text.

rules.title: Slow, confident motion
rules.body: Entrances rise 20–50px and fade over 0.8–1s on cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), staggered 0.1–0.2s. The hero's slide uses 2.8s on cubic-bezier(0.19, 1, 0.22, 1). Hover changes take about 300ms, card washes about 500ms. Honour reduced motion with useReducedMotionConfig().

rules.title: Outfit belongs to the tools
rules.body: The admin dashboard uses Outfit (variable, 100–900) for everything; it is the interface font here (font-interface). Use it for dense screens such as tables, dashboards and the app's earnings figures. Customer-facing copy stays Playfair and DM Sans. The admin's own colours are not part of this system, and nor is the app's Montserrat.

rules.title: Orbitron is for card numbers
rules.body: The app sets payment-card digits in Orbitron with wide tracking; it is the mono face here (font-mono). Keep it to short technical strings such as card numbers and codes, never paragraphs or labels.

rules.title: Two quiet button fills
rules.body: Beside a primary action, the app uses two filled buttons with rounded-inset corners and DM Sans semibold labels: tonal, a blue-slate (#323743) with off-white text, for things like Earnings; and secondary, a mid grey (#5E5E5E) with white text, for things like Edit Profile. Both hold their colour in light and dark.

items.name: theme-studio
items.title: Studio (bash-ui)
items.description: A composed frame for expressive detail. Layered dark surfaces, softly lit controls and quiet typography create depth while giving colour, shape and movement room to be noticed.
items.docs: Load the fonts with next/font: Inter({ variable: "--font-inter" }); Roboto_Mono({ variable: "--font-roboto-mono" }). Rules: https://bash-ui-registry.vercel.app/systems/studio

rules.title: Surfaces, not borders
rules.body: A panel is a step lighter than what it sits on, at 16px. No outline. Depth comes from the surface, not from a line around it.

rules.title: Raised means lit from above
rules.body: A selected or pressable chip gets a white 6–8% fill, a one-pixel inset highlight on its top edge and a tight drop shadow. Never a border.

rules.title: Everything you press is a pill
rules.body: Nav, tabs, actions and arrows are fully rounded, 30–36px tall, 13px medium text. Square corners are for content, round ones for controls.

rules.title: Two greys of text
rules.body: Near-white for what you read, a mid grey (#979797) for everything else. Labels are 11px and quiet, never uppercase.

rules.title: One blue, rarely
rules.body: The accent is a single blue, used for links, focus and the one call to action. Everything else is greyscale.

items.name: theme-neutral
items.title: Neutral (bash-ui)
items.description: A clear, adaptable foundation. Balanced greys, straightforward typography and a measured indigo accent give proportion, hierarchy and interaction space to speak for themselves.
items.docs: Load the fonts with next/font: Geist({ variable: "--font-geist-sans" }); Geist_Mono({ variable: "--font-geist-mono" }). Rules: https://bash-ui-registry.vercel.app/systems/neutral

rules.title: Nothing to prove
rules.body: No brand, no warmth. Every component should still read clearly here; if it does not, it is depending on a colour it never asked for.

items.name: account-menu
items.title: Account menu
items.description: The account block at the foot of an app rail: avatar, name and role, opening upward into a frosted menu with the email, a highlight that slides between rows, icons that gesture as it lands, and a red Log out.

meta.whenToUse: Use for the signed-in person's own menu (profile, settings, help, sign out) at the foot or top of a sidebar or header. Do not use for menus about content on the page, or for more than a handful of rows; that is a plain dropdown or a settings page.

credits.name: Animate UI (Radix Dropdown Menu, Highlight, animated icons)

items.name: ai-cost-card
items.title: AI cost card
items.description: A spend card for estimated AI cost: the window's total with its change on the prior stretch, a 7D–ALL window switch, the split by kind of work as horizontal sticks with a figure legend, and one stacked-stick column per date that fills up bottom to top.

meta.whenToUse: Use to watch a metered cost (AI tokens, API calls, SMS) over several windows where the reader asks both how much and on what. Not for a single figure with no breakdown (use a metric card), and not as an invoice: it is built to say its numbers are estimates and floors.

credits.name: Lucide loader-pinwheel icon (paths), animated as in Animate UI's icon
Animate UI (spin-on-hover icon behaviour)

items.name: app-sidebar
items.title: App sidebar
items.description: A frosted app rail: logo and name, labelled sections of nav rows with count pills, a slot for a checklist, a footer with a theme switch, and the account menu. It collapses to icons with tooltips on desktop and becomes a focus-trapping drawer on a phone.

meta.whenToUse: Use as the persistent primary navigation of a signed-in app with five to fifteen destinations. Do not use for a marketing site's header, for in-page section tabs, or for settings sub-navigation inside a page.

credits.name: Animate UI (Radix Tooltip, animated icons)
AnimateIcons (row-hover icon animation)

items.name: app-store-badge
items.title: App store badge
items.description: A two-line App Store or Google Play badge in the theme's ink: the store's glyph, a small lead-in and the store's name, solid or outlined.

meta.whenToUse: Use on a landing or download page to send people to an app's store listing; place one per store side by side. Apple's and Google's marketing guidelines may require their official badge artwork for store listings and adverts, so swap in the official badges where those guidelines apply.

origin.path: src/components/ui/contact-form.jsx (App Store and Google Play image badges; redrawn in theme tokens for bash-ui)

credits.name: Simple Icons: Apple and Google Play glyphs (trademarks of Apple Inc. and Google LLC)

items.name: arrow-button
items.title: Arrow button
items.description: A pill whose small dot blooms to fill it on hover while the label slides out and returns beside an up-right arrow in inverted colours, without the pill changing width.

meta.whenToUse: Use for a page's main outbound call to action, such as Download or Sign up: solid in the hero, outlined in the navigation. Do not use for form submits or dense app toolbars; the bloom is a marketing flourish and loses its point when repeated.

credits.name: Magic UI, Interactive Hover Button (dot bloom and label swap; Steeze added the in-flow sizer, outline variant and up-right arrow)

items.name: breakdown-dial
items.title: Breakdown dial
items.description: A card with a 270° dial of 42 ticks split between a few groups, the total in its centre, and a row per group with its count and share; hovering a group isolates its ticks.

meta.whenToUse: Use to show how one whole divides into three to five ranked groups (priority bands, statuses) at a glance, with the exact counts beside it. Not for values over time or for more than about five groups; use a chart or a list for those.

items.name: checkbox
items.title: Checkbox
items.description: An animated checkbox: the box springs on hover and press, fills with the lead colour, and the tick draws itself in.

meta.whenToUse: Use for any yes/no or multi-select choice instead of a native checkbox, which ignores theme tokens. Pair it with a <label htmlFor>; for a single on/off setting that takes effect immediately, a switch reads better.

credits.name: Animate UI (Radix Checkbox)

items.name: count-tabs
items.title: Count tabs
items.description: An underlined tab row where each tab carries a count chip, the open tab in the lead colour with a 2px underline on the row's rule and its chip on the lead wash.

meta.whenToUse: Use to switch between queues or lists on one page where how many items wait in each is the point (a review page, an inbox's folders). Not for page-level section navigation between routes; use gooey-tabs or a link row for that.

items.name: cta-button
items.title: CTA button
items.description: A glass label pill and an accent disc touching at one point; on hover the pair lifts, the disc swallows its ring, the accent washes across the label and the arrow loops through the disc.

meta.whenToUse: Use for the single action that matters on a public or marketing screen (Get started, Go to app, Log in), one per screen. Do not use inside a dense app screen or for secondary actions; the effect is a signature and wears out when repeated.

items.name: date-range-calendar
items.title: Date range calendar
items.description: A Monday-first range calendar that previews the span under the cursor, greys out days outside its bounds and jumps by month or typed year; plus a period dropdown whose "Custom range" step widens the same popover into the calendar.

meta.whenToUse: Use for picking a reporting window or a single due date inside a card or popover, especially where a native date input would close its parent on blur or format to the wrong locale. Use DateRangePicker when presets cover most needs and exact dates are the exception; not for date-and-time entry or recurring schedules.

origin.path: src/components/ui/date-range-calendar.tsx (rules from src/lib/date-range.ts); popover from PeriodSelect in src/components/ui/metric-controls.tsx

items.name: delete-button
items.title: Delete button
items.description: A two-step delete (Delete, then Confirm with an X to back out) that ends in a Thanos snap: the button tears into dust through an SVG displacement filter. Ships with ThanosSnapEffect, a wrapper that snaps anything else the same way.

meta.whenToUse: Use for deleting one row, card or version in place, where a modal confirm would be heavy and the user should feel the thing go. Remove the row in onComplete, never in onConfirm. Not for bulk deletes, for anything that cannot be undone and deserves a typed confirmation, or inside a container that clips overflow tightly, which cuts the dust off.

credits.name: Mikhail Bespalov, "Thanos snap" dissolve CodePen (the displacement-filter dissolve)

items.name: dissolve-input
items.title: Dissolve input
items.description: Ledge’s underlined login input, whose text dissolves into particles from right to left with a visible action button, on Enter or after a confirmed action.

meta.whenToUse: Use for a single-value submission or a success transition. Enter previews the effect; in a login form set dissipateOnEnter={false} and call ref.dissipate() only after authentication succeeds. Completion clears the controlled value, allowing another attempt.

items.name: donut-chart
items.title: Donut chart
items.description: Ledge’s collection doughnut paired with exact amounts and percentages on the right, plus linked slice and legend highlights.

meta.whenToUse: Use to show how collected money is divided. Pass integer kobo and ensure landlord net + platform retained + processing fees equals gross.

items.name: doodle-portrait
items.title: Doodle portrait
items.description: A portrait framed by the original animated doodle in the top left and its rotated copy in the bottom right.

meta.whenToUse: Use for a personal introduction. Supply a portrait and decorative artwork; include a static doodle frame for reduced motion.

items.name: expanding-menu
items.title: Expanding menu
items.description: Ledge’s frosted navigation pill expands into a staggered link panel; the plus becomes a minus.

meta.whenToUse: Use for compact shared navigation. Preserves Ledge’s 148×56 pill, 300px panel, fixed 28px corners, frosted layers, spring timing and staggered links; supports a footer slot.

items.name: faq-accordion
items.title: FAQ accordion
items.description: A question-and-answer accordion whose organic, hand-cut plus turns its upright bar flat into a minus as the answer unblurs open beneath it.

meta.whenToUse: Use for FAQs and other short, scannable question lists where each answer is a paragraph or two. Do not use it to hide primary content or long forms; anything most readers need should be visible without a press.

credits.name: The Rest Is History club FAQ: plus and minus bar artwork (the SVG path matches therestishistory.com/club exactly)
shadcn/ui Accordion (Root, Item, Trigger and Content structure over Radix)

items.name: feedback-card
items.title: Feedback card
items.description: A non-blocking card that floats at the bottom right and asks for a 1–5 rating on a morphing face, with an optional comment, then thanks the person and leaves.

meta.whenToUse: Use to ask for an occasional in-product rating without interrupting work; the caller decides when it shows. Do not use for a required form, a bug report with fields, or anything that must block the page; use a dialog for those.

credits.name: Spectrum UI (Face Rating)

items.name: feedback-sheet
items.title: Feedback sheet
items.description: A tall bottom sheet that is almost all text field: write, send with a full-width pill, or follow a quiet link. It slides up over a dimmed page and drags down to dismiss.

meta.whenToUse: Use for open-ended feedback or a quick note from anywhere in an app, where a full page would be too much. Not for structured surveys or ratings; use a form or the feedback card for those.

credits.name: @gorhom/bottom-sheet: the app's sheet behaviour (handle, pan-down to close, backdrop) re-created here with motion and Radix Dialog

items.name: funnel-chart
items.title: Funnel chart
items.description: Pipeline stage totals above a pale curved funnel, with vertical guides and percentage pills.

meta.whenToUse: Use to show how a starting population progresses through ordered stages. Percentages on the ribbon compare with the first stage; summary percentages compare with the previous stage.

items.name: github-activity-chart
items.title: GitHub activity chart
items.description: A watercolour contribution calendar with painted cells, subtle splatters, day inspection and a five-level activity legend.

meta.whenToUse: Use for dated activity counts. Supply contribution data from any source; this component performs no requests. The preview uses deterministic example data, not a live GitHub account.

items.name: gooey-input
items.title: Gooey input
items.description: A pill text field whose submit button is a droplet of the same liquid: on focus it pulls away from the capsule through a gooey SVG bridge and lands beside it with its icon.

meta.whenToUse: Reach for it for a single-value action field that deserves a moment of delight: a sign-up email, a URL to import, an inline rename. Not for multi-field forms, where a plain input and one submit button read better, and not inside overflow-hidden containers that would clip the droplet's travel.

credits.name: liquid-gooey by Jakub Antalik (goo filter, silhouette/content layering, shadow-on-merged-silhouette passes)

items.name: gooey-tabs
items.title: Gooey tabs
items.description: A floating segmented pill of equal-width tabs whose solid marker slides to the picked tab while a liquid silhouette chases it on a spring, stretching and trailing a droplet tail.

meta.whenToUse: Use as the primary section switcher at the top of a record or detail page with three to six sections, where each tab can be a route (pass href) or local state. Not for long or variable-length labels (every tab is one width) or for a queue switcher that needs counts as the main signal; use count-tabs for that.

credits.name: liquid-gooey by Jakub Antalik (the Liquid move effect, used as a dependency)

items.name: image-collage
items.title: Image collage
items.description: A responsive image collage with proportionate widths, aligned image heights and captions. Every row fills the available width.

meta.whenToUse: Use to show school, employer or project images upright without decorative framing. Images share a height within each row, and a final single image fills the row. Supply aspect ratios for stable layout before loading, plus optional captions and descriptions.

origin.path: src/app/page.tsx (education, experience and project imagery; composed into a collage for bash-ui)

items.name: inbox-button
items.title: Inbox button
items.description: A shortcut button to an inbox whose tray glyph dips and redraws on hover or focus, with a slim four-colour provider rail along its bottom edge and an optional unread count.

meta.whenToUse: Use as the one way into a mail inbox from a dashboard or header, where naming the mail provider by colour helps. Do not use for general navigation; a plain link or nav item is quieter.

credits.name: AnimateIcons (Avijit Dey), lucide/inbox-icon animation
Lucide, inbox icon paths

items.name: income-spending-chart
items.title: Income vs spending chart
items.description: A financial history chart with a smooth trend strip, paired segmented bars, signed net results and year tooltips.

meta.whenToUse: Use to compare income and spending across filed years. Missing amounts remain distinct from zero; net results have a separate scale.

items.name: info-tooltip
items.title: Info tooltip
items.description: An (i) icon that springs open an inverted tooltip with an optional title and footer; opens on tap on a phone.

meta.whenToUse: Use to explain a label, metric or setting in a sentence or two without cluttering the screen, or wrap any element to give it a hover hint. Do not put actions or anything the reader must see inside it; that belongs in a popover or on the page.

credits.name: Animate UI (Radix Tooltip)

items.name: key-login-button
items.title: Key login button
items.description: Ledge’s green pill login button with a rotating key and rolling label on hover or keyboard focus.

meta.whenToUse: Use as an entry action or login link. Supply href for navigation, or onClick / type="submit" for an action.

items.name: link-preview
items.title: Link preview
items.description: A text trigger reveals a screenshot of the destination webpage on hover, keyboard focus or tap. The screenshot fills the card; its address rises in on a frosted chip once the pointer is on it.

meta.whenToUse: Use for portfolios, references and policy summaries where readers benefit from context before navigating. Supply a screenshot of the page; this component does not capture websites or fetch metadata. Keep essential information available on the destination page.

items.name: loading-button
items.title: Loading button
items.description: A compact solid button for one async job: its icon spins and its label swaps while the work runs, then a short go or stop status line says how it went.

meta.whenToUse: Use for an on-demand fetch, refresh or re-check the user triggers mid-task, where the outcome is worth a one-line answer. Do not use for form submission or navigation, or for data the page needs to render; fetch that on the page.

items.name: lock-toggle
items.title: Lock toggle
items.description: A Material Design 3 switch in the theme's tokens whose knob carries a lock when on and an open lock when off, with M3's spring slide, growing knob, rotating icon and pointer halo.

meta.whenToUse: Use where flipping it is the save: a protection or setting that applies at once, especially one where turning it off is the risky direction (the default stop tone). Control it with `checked` to hold it on until a confirmation lands. Not for answers in a form submitted later; use a checkbox.

credits.name: Material Design 3 Switch by Hossain Jahed (EaseMize UI), copied as-is from 21st.dev and restyled with bash-ui tokens. 21st.dev lists its licence as unknown
Material Design 3: Switch (design spec)

items.name: metric-card
items.title: Metric card
items.description: A headline metric card with a smooth line (or bar) chart washed into its right side, a trend badge coloured by direction, a line/bar toggle, and a period dropdown with an optional custom-range calendar.

meta.whenToUse: Use for one headline number that moves over time (a total, a daily count) where the reader wants the figure first and the shape second, with hover to read any day. Not for comparing many categories or for a table of figures; use a bar chart or a list for those.

items.name: money-flow-chart
items.title: Money flow chart
items.description: Income ribbons converge on a pooled fund and flow out to spending, with year selection, hover tracing and pinned bands.

meta.whenToUse: Use for balanced money flows through a shared pot. Each side must sum to total; include a surplus or reserves band to balance the year. It does not claim which source funded which activity.

credits.name: liquid-gooey

items.name: notification-toggle
items.title: Notification toggle
items.description: Steeze's SMS notification switch: a pale knob on a grey track when off, a charcoal knob on lilac when on, adapted from React Native to a keyboard-accessible web control.

meta.whenToUse: Use for notification preferences and other settings that apply immediately. Pass checked and onCheckedChange for caller-owned state, or defaultChecked for an uncontrolled switch. Supply aria-label or aria-labelledby.

credits.name: React Native Switch: the mobile app's native control, re-created for the web

items.name: pipeline-chart
items.title: Pipeline chart
items.description: A chart card that plots several pipeline stages (contacted, replied, converted) over time on real axes, with a per-stage legend that doubles as the summary, a line/bar toggle, a crosshair tooltip and a period dropdown that opens a custom-range calendar.

meta.whenToUse: Use to compare a few daily counts over a reader-chosen window, where each line needs its own figure and change against the window before. Not for a single KPI with a sparkline (use a stat tile), for more than about five series, or for non-time categorical comparisons (use a bar chart).

origin.path: src/components/ui/series-line-chart-card.tsx (ViewToggle from src/components/ui/metric-controls.tsx); used as "Contacted, replied, converted" in src/components/dashboard/performance-section.tsx

items.name: qr-code
items.title: QR code
items.description: Steeze's QR code artwork with no background of its own: cream modules in dark mode, inverted to dark modules in light mode.

meta.whenToUse: Use to hand a link from a desktop screen to a phone, such as an app download or a sign-up page. Pass your own code artwork as light modules on a transparent ground, leave the page around it clear, and keep it above about 120px so it scans.

origin.path: src/components/ui/contact-form.jsx (public/assets/branding/qrcode.webp, its charcoal ground made transparent for bash-ui)

items.name: radial-nav
items.title: Radial navigation
items.description: Portfolio’s original radial navigation: selected-only expanding labels, a shortest-path spring pointer, and ring and pointer emphasis during rotation.

meta.whenToUse: Use for compact section navigation. Choose inline or collapsible presentation; handle navigation and scroll tracking through activeId and onActiveChange in the consuming page.

credits.name: Animate UI community Radial Nav by arhamkhnz

items.name: range-slider
items.title: Range slider
items.description: A two-thumb range slider over a histogram whose bars, inside the range, run red on the left to green on the right, with the minimum and maximum read out large beneath it; plus a single-value stick slider on the same ramp.

meta.whenToUse: Reach for it when a filter is a numeric range where low-to-high also reads bad-to-good or small-to-large (income, budget, size), especially with a distribution worth showing; pass `stops` for a non-linear scale. Not for picking one value from a short list (use a select or segmented control), and not where red/green would imply a judgement the data does not make (use colorScheme="primary").

items.name: ranking-table
items.title: Ranking table
items.description: A landlord ranking with a sentence-style measure picker, direction toggle, sortable columns and mobile cards.

meta.whenToUse: Use for comparing landlord collections and platform fees. Sorting stays local to the supplied rows, with optional row destinations supplied by the caller.

items.name: revenue-bar-chart
items.title: Revenue bar chart
items.description: Monthly stacked revenue bars split between platform net and processing fees, with a toggle to include landlord payments.

meta.whenToUse: Use to inspect platform revenue over time. The landlord toggle rescales to gross collections; each amount is integer kobo.

items.name: saved-board
items.title: Saved board
items.description: A saved-items board as a frosted pocket: up to five covers fan out of the top and bob gently on their own beats, with the board's name, owner and item count on the glass.

meta.whenToUse: Use for collections people make and share, such as boards, wishlists or lookbooks, in a carousel or grid where the covers should do the talking. Not for a single product; use an ordinary product card for that.

credits.name: Steeze category photos, found on Pinterest (original photographers unknown); preview fixtures only, not shipped

items.name: score-gauge
items.title: Score gauge
items.description: A 0–1 score as an instrument gauge: a 250° comb of bars in a stop-to-go gradient, divided into named zones, with a tapered needle that springs in to the reading.

meta.whenToUse: Reach for it when one bounded score (priority, fit, health) needs to be read against its whole scale, at full size with per-zone explanations in a record header or as a mini dial on list cards. Not for unbounded numbers, trends over time, or comparing several scores side by side.

items.name: scramble-text
items.title: Scramble text
items.description: A wordmark that scrambles into place a letter at a time, flashes a decoy word that is struck out, then rises in for good.

meta.whenToUse: Use once, for a brand moment: a splash screen, the first sight of a wordmark, a reveal on a landing page. Allow room for its 10vh entrance. At the default pace it settles after 2.6 seconds.

origin.path: src/App.jsx (splash: splashReducer, scrambleWords and the scramble/strike/after phases)

items.name: search-bar
items.title: Search bar
items.description: A pill search field with a cycling prompt that unfolds into a staged filter panel, with an optional plain-English ask field and removable filter chips.

meta.whenToUse: Reach for it as the one search control at the top of a list page, where people combine a name search with several filters and submit them together. Not for instant as-you-type filtering, inline table search, or a compact toolbar field: nothing is reported until Enter or the disc is pressed, and the open panel needs about 350px of room below it.

items.name: searchable-select
items.title: Searchable select
items.description: A single-choice dropdown with a search field above a grouped, scrollable list of options.

meta.whenToUse: Use for choosing one client, place or category from a long list. Filters immediately by label, group or keywords; supports arrow keys, Enter and Escape.

items.name: send-button
items.title: Send button
items.description: A send button whose paper plane bobs, turns and flies forward on hover as the label slides out behind it, with a pending state that holds the plane still.

meta.whenToUse: Use for the one action on a screen that sends something out of the app: an email, a message, an invitation. Do not use it for ordinary saves or submits; the flourish only means something if it is rare.

credits.name: adamgiebl, "Send" paper plane button on Uiverse.io (hover choreography: fly-1 bob, 45° turn, label slide)

items.name: social-links
items.title: Social link buttons
items.description: Watercolour GitHub and LinkedIn buttons with transparent artwork, generous spacing, accessible labels and configurable link targets.

meta.whenToUse: Use when custom image artwork is the social link itself. Supply your own artwork URLs and destinations.

items.name: sort-by-heading
items.title: Sort-by heading
items.description: An editorial heading that reads “Top landlords by [platform fee]”, followed by a direction toggle.

meta.whenToUse: Use when the ranking criterion belongs in the heading. A custom dropdown preserves the sentence-like appearance, with keyboard selection, a checked item, Escape and click-away dismissal.

items.name: stick-progress-bar
items.title: Stick progress bar
items.description: A progress bar drawn as a row of vertical sticks that grow in one after another, as one value against a total or as a split into coloured segments, with a hover tooltip.

meta.whenToUse: Reach for it to show a share of a whole on a card: progress against a limit, a split of spending, a count toward a milestone (with a position-fixed colour ramp). Not for values over time or comparisons of many series; use a chart for those.

items.name: swipe-cards
items.title: Swipe cards
items.description: A stack of photo cards to swipe right to like or left to skip: the card tilts as it travels, a stamp and the matching button fill in near the commit point, and the cards behind rise to take its place.

meta.whenToUse: Use for fast, one-at-a-time judgements over visual items: a discovery feed, a taste survey, tuning recommendations. Not for anything people need to compare side by side or come back to; a swipe is gone. Buttons and the arrow keys do the same as a drag.

credits.name: Steeze category photos, found on Pinterest (original photographers unknown); gallery preview only, not shipped

items.name: tech-stack
items.title: Tech stack logos
items.description: A tilted, overlapping stack of technology logos that fans out on hover or focus and shows each logo’s label in a tooltip.

meta.whenToUse: Use beside project descriptions to list technologies. Logos and text are props; hover, keyboard focus and touch reveal the details.

credits.name: Technology brand logos from Wikimedia Commons and Icons8, preview fixtures only (per-file licences not recorded; Icons8's free licence requires a link back)

items.name: todo-list
items.title: To-do list
items.description: A compact checklist card with an n-of-m count and springy progress bar, where a done step's tick pops in and a hand-drawn scribble strikes its title through.

meta.whenToUse: Use for a short list of steps to finish, such as onboarding or prep for a task, in a sidebar or beside the work; ticks can be read-only (marked done elsewhere) or tickable. Do not use for long or sortable task lists, or for multi-select in a form; use a table or the checkbox primitive.

items.name: tonal-button
items.title: Tonal button
items.description: A filled secondary button in two quiet fills: a tinted tonal fill and a neutral secondary one, as in Steeze's Earnings and Edit Profile pair.

meta.whenToUse: Use for actions that sit beside or below a primary one and still need to read as buttons, such as profile shortcuts or a pair of settings. Not for the main call to action on a screen, and not for destructive actions.

origin.path: app_steeze: app/(root)/(tabs)/profile.tsx (Earnings and Edit Profile buttons)

items.name: video-button
items.title: Video button
items.description: A button with theme-specific resting colours that reveals a looping clip or GIF on hover, under a dark scrim with a light label.

meta.whenToUse: Use for one playful, low-stakes action with personality, such as Get in touch at the end of an FAQ. Do not use for primary flows or repeated actions; the media is a flourish and costs bandwidth.

credits.name: GIPHY clip used on steeze.ng (creator not recorded; GIPHY's terms cover embedding through GIPHY, not rehosting the file); gallery preview only, not shipped

items.name: wallet-card
items.title: Wallet card
items.description: A payment card that slides into a stitched leather pocket and peeks out above it, with the balance counting up in the pocket behind an eye toggle. Tap the card to pull it up.

meta.whenToUse: Use as the hero of an earnings or wallet screen, where one balance matters and the card is the user's identity in the product. Not for lists of accounts or several balances; it is one object, and it needs about 340px of width and 330px of height.

credits.name: "The New Home and Colonial Offices, Westminster, 1875", Wellcome Collection: the engraved card artwork, changes made; gallery preview only, not shipped
